item.title: Mistral releases Large 4, a 49B-parameter multimodal model with 1.6B vision encoder and Mixture-of-Experts architecture [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Mistral has introduced Large 4, an open-weight, general-purpose multimodal AI model featuring 49 billion active parameters and a total of 1.05 trillion parameters. The model incorporates a 1.6 billion parameter vision encoder and uses a granular Mixture-of-Experts architecture to enhance performance across tasks. Large 4 is designed to handle diverse input and output token types, supporting advanced multimodal applications. It represents Mistral's latest advancement in large-scale AI models, following previous releases such as Z.ai GLM 5.3 and Shieldstral 1.0, and is documented in detail on Mistral's official website.

item.title: Mistral launches Mistral Large 4, a 1 trillion-parameter multimodal AI model with 49 billion active parameters, offering state-of-the-art open-weight performance and cybersecurity capabilities [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Mistral has introduced Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a 1 trillion-parameter multimodal AI model with 49 billion active parameters, available now in public preview via Mistral Studio. ML4 demonstrates competitive performance across coding, agentic workflows, and multimodal understanding, surpassing other open-weight models in cybersecurity, finance, and law, and even outperforming some closed models in visual grounding. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in European data centers, ML4 supports AI sovereignty with open weights and self-deployment options, enabling organizations to maintain control over AI capabilities, especially in sensitive areas like cybersecurity. The model will be available globally, including a fully European deployment under European law, and supports over 160 languages. Mistral plans to release the model weights by the end of the month and will provide further details on architecture and benchmarks as development continues.

item.title: Opus 5.5 AI agents identify two candidate room-temperature magnetic semiconductors with potential spintronic applications [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A team using Opus 5.5 AI agents has discovered two candidate materials for room-temperature magnetic semiconductors, which could advance spintronic technology by enabling efficient electron spin sorting without macroscopic magnetic fields. One candidate was newly designed by the AI agents, while the other was first synthesized in 1999 and predicted by calculations to have the desired properties. The research focuses on materials that combine features of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, specifically Luttinger compensated magnets, which allow spin-up and spin-down electrons to be sorted by energy despite having zero net magnetic moment. This property could improve data storage speed and density by overcoming limitations of traditional magnetic materials used in spintronics.

item.title: Reflection introduces Beam, a 501 billion parameter open-weight sparse Mixture-of-Experts model optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks with high compute reinforcement learning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Reflection has launched Beam, its first open-weight model featuring 501 billion total parameters with 23 billion active, designed for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam was pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens from diverse, high-quality datasets and underwent extensive reinforcement learning using 10.5K NVIDIA GPUs over four weeks, achieving competitive performance with greater inference efficiency compared to similar-sized open models. Beam emphasizes efficiency and capability, delivering strong coding and reasoning performance while using 3 to 4 times less inference compute than comparable models. The model incorporates a controllable reasoning effort parameter allowing users to balance response length and performance. Reflection plans to release Beam's weights, technical report, and developer tools later this month after final evaluations and red-teaming.

item.title: OpenChart launches open-source TradingView alternative with integrated AI agents for market analysis and alerts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenChart is an open-source desktop application offering a TradingView alternative that integrates AI agents for statistical and technical market analysis, real-time alerts, and opportunity discovery. Users can deploy their own AI models like Claude, Codex, and Gemini to customize research, indicators, and alerts without software quotas on charts or indicators. The platform supports a custom programming language called Tea for building market logic and is designed for self-hosting with optional cloud market data pricing. OpenChart aims to explore collaborative asset management between humans and AI agents and invites community contributions and feedback through GitHub and Discord.

item.title: AI whistleblowers say researchers are checking AI-generated code less frequently as AI leads more than a quarter of model research at Anthropic [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Three former AI researchers testified at a New York City Council hearing that AI labs have increasingly allowed AI to drive coding and research processes, resulting in less frequent human checks of AI-generated work. The whistleblowers, formerly of Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind, highlighted changes in AI research practices that may affect oversight and quality control. Anthropic reported that as of August, AI was leading over 25% of its model research and development, reflecting a broader trend of AI accelerating research workflows. Representatives from the AI labs did not directly address the whistleblowers' claims during the hearing.

item.title: LibreOffice commits to no AI integration in default software to protect user privacy and data control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The Document Foundation, which develops the open source LibreOffice document editor, announced it will not include AI features in its default software configuration to ensure user privacy and data security. The organization emphasized that LibreOffice does not upload documents to external servers and functions without requiring a network connection, allowing users to retain full control over their data. LibreOffice allows users to add AI capabilities through optional extensions that connect to local AI models, but the foundation currently sees no AI integration meeting its criteria for privacy and independence from single AI providers. This stance contrasts with many software makers who are rapidly incorporating AI features, often involving data processing on remote servers.

item.title: Workday faces growth constraints as AI tools from Anthropic and Microsoft enable customers to access data without using its core apps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Workday's enterprise applications remain essential for storing employee and financial data, but AI technologies are limiting their growth potential. Some customers use AI agents from providers like Anthropic and Microsoft to extract and analyze Workday data directly, reducing the need to interact with Workday's own interface. Additionally, many companies with access to Workday's AI-enhanced tools reportedly do not use them regularly, according to consultants working with thousands of Workday clients.

item.title: Mistral AI launches Mistral Large 4, a 1 trillion parameter multimodal model aiming to surpass US and Chinese AI rivals with planned open-weight release [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: French AI lab Mistral AI has introduced Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a large multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters designed to compete with both American and Chinese AI models. The model is currently accessible via a public endpoint, with plans to release its open weights after safety testing in three weeks. ML4 was trained using Mistral's own compute resources, significantly fewer GPUs than competitors, and targets applications in cybersecurity, finance, and chip design. Mistral positions ML4 as a European alternative amid the divide between closed and open AI models, aiming to offer a secure and auditable solution for enterprises and institutions.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740M-parameter open multimodal embedding model optimized for on-device inference and privacy-first applications [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google DeepMind introduced EmbeddingGemma 2, an open-source multimodal embedding model that unifies text, images, audio, and video into a shared embedding space for on-device use. The model, built on the Gemma 4 architecture with 740 million parameters, supports efficient local processing with a focus on privacy, enabling applications like semantic search and retrieval across multiple data types without cloud dependency. EmbeddingGemma 2 offers modular design with optional encoders for vision and audio, supports dynamic vector dimension reduction for storage efficiency, and features an extended 8K token context window for processing longer inputs. It achieves top-tier performance on benchmarks for code, vision, and audio tasks among sub-1B parameter models, and is optimized to run within tight resource constraints on devices such as the Google Pixel 11 Pro. The model facilitates on-device retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines when paired with generative models like Gemma 4, enabling complex multimodal understanding and real-time decision-making. Developers can access the model weights on platforms like Hugging Face and Kaggle, with tools and APIs provided to support deployment and integration in privacy-sensitive applications.

item.title: US executive order mandates replacing 'Artificial Intelligence' with 'Super Intelligence' despite no change in technology definition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A US executive order signed on September 29, 2026, requires federal agencies to use the term "Super Intelligence" (SI) instead of "Artificial Intelligence" (AI) in all official communications, arguing that current AI systems exceed mere imitation of human intelligence. Despite the renaming, the legal definition remains unchanged, describing SI as machine-based systems that make predictions or decisions based on human-defined objectives, identical to the previous AI definition. The change reflects a broader trend in Silicon Valley, with companies like Meta and Microsoft adopting the term "superintelligence" for their AI initiatives. However, in AI research, superintelligence still refers to a hypothetical machine surpassing human capabilities across virtually all tasks, which has not yet been achieved. The article also discusses the symbolic implications of renaming AI to SI, comparing it to historical examples of misattributed creation and emphasizing that current AI systems are fundamentally human-made.

item.title: Study finds newer Frontier AI models generate funnier original jokes, with GPT-6, Fable 5.1, and Opus 4.5 outperforming earlier versions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluated the humor capabilities of six Frontier AI language models by having human raters assess original jokes generated using random word pairs. The experiment aimed to determine if advances in AI's verifiable skills like math and coding also translate to subjective domains such as joke creation. Results showed that larger, more recent models like GPT-6, Fable 5.1, and Opus 4.5 produced jokes rated as funnier compared to older or smaller models. The study used blind human ratings to compare jokes and enforced originality by requiring specific word inclusion, avoiding country-specific references. This suggests AI humor is improving over time, though challenges remain in ensuring truly original and universally funny content.

item.title: Pinterest launches AI-powered Beauty Guides to translate hair and nail Pins into salon terminology with cost, time, and maintenance details [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Pinterest introduced Beauty Guides, an AI feature that converts saved beauty Pins into actionable salon plans by translating styles into professional terms like balayage and almond nails. The guides provide users with estimated appointment durations, price ranges, and maintenance advice to help plan salon visits. The feature integrates Pinterest's visual intelligence and generative AI technology, Pinterest Intelligence, and is accessible via a "Get the Guide" button on relevant Pins. At launch, it supports hairstyle, color, nail shape, and finish Pins, aiming to make salon consultations more informed and efficient.

item.title: Ghost raises $11M seed round to build Core, a $3,499 personal AI computer with integrated Nvidia GPU and local data processing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Zain Javaid, a 19-year-old founder, has raised $11 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz for Ghost, a startup developing Core, a personal AI computer priced at $3,499. Core is designed to run AI agents locally, centralizing user data and automating tasks through continuous AI processing without relying on cloud services. Core includes an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 GPU and preinstalled AI models, with users able to add or update models via over-the-air updates. The device operates without a screen and is accessed through a phone or app, emphasizing user data privacy by encrypting all information locally. Ghost plans to begin shipping Core units in late October from its San Francisco facility.

item.title: Google Earth AI helps public health officials forecast disease outbreaks and identify at-risk populations using satellite imagery and geospatial models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google is using artificial intelligence combined with satellite imagery to assist public health leaders in predicting disease outbreaks, overcoming reporting delays, and delivering care to vulnerable communities worldwide. The technology enables faster mapping of at-risk populations and forecasting of health trends compared to traditional methods. Researchers and health professionals can request free access to these data insights or apply for Google Earth credits to support local health initiatives. The tools have been applied during the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where they helped identify remote high-risk areas and estimate the risk of disease spread into uninfected zones. By integrating environmental signals, mobility data, and foundation models, Google Earth AI provides public health teams with advanced predictive capabilities to complement existing health information and shift emergency response from reactive to proactive management.

item.title: US Appeals Court Rules Using Copyrighted Material for AI Training Is Not Fair Use in Ross Intelligence Case [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A US appeals court upheld a ruling that AI legal research company Ross Intelligence violated copyright law by training its search engine on Thomson Reuters' Westlaw materials, rejecting the fair use defense. The court found Ross copied editorial summaries verbatim to develop a competing tool, which was deemed non-transformative and thus not protected under fair use. This decision marks a significant moment in ongoing legal battles between AI companies and rights holders over unauthorized use of copyrighted content for AI training. While the ruling is specific to Ross Intelligence's case, industry reactions suggest it may not broadly preclude transformative AI training, and further lawsuits, including one against Anthropic, are pending to clarify the legal landscape for generative AI models.

item.title: Kuaishou's AI unit Kling selects banks for Hong Kong IPO targeting over $1 billion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Kling AI, a spinoff from Chinese video app Kuaishou Technology that develops AI video generation models, has chosen banks to manage its initial public offering in Hong Kong, aiming to raise at least $1 billion. The company plans to list as soon as next year. This move marks a significant step for Kling as it seeks to expand its presence in the AI and video technology markets.

item.title: Mistral launches Large 4, a trillion-parameter AI model trained in Europe focused on cybersecurity tasks avoided by US models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Mistral has introduced Large 4, its largest AI model with one trillion parameters, trained on European infrastructure and designed to handle cybersecurity tasks that US models like Claude and GPT-6 avoid due to safety filters. The model is currently available in preview via Mistral Studio, with full weights expected by the end of October. An independent Intelligence Index scores Large 4 at 38 points, a significant improvement over previous Mistral models but still behind leading closed models such as Claude Opus 5.5. Large 4 excels in reproducing and patching software vulnerabilities, scoring 82 percent on a cybersecurity benchmark where competitors score near zero because they refuse such tasks. Mistral emphasizes that this capability addresses a gap in security research, as closed models block vulnerability work despite attackers exploiting them. The model also performs well in coding and image understanding benchmarks and is designed to run in private clouds or on-premises, supporting European data sovereignty. Mistral is currently collaborating with security firms, partners, and government agencies to test and refine Large 4, aiming to balance security capabilities with high refusal rates on malicious prompts. The company positions Large 4 as a European alternative to US and Chinese AI models, particularly for sensitive cybersecurity applications where access to open-weight models is critical.

item.title: Google limits free Gemini users to Flash Lite model starting October 9; Pro and standard Flash access require paid AI Plus or higher subscriptions [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Starting October 9, Google will restrict free users of its Gemini AI to the Flash Lite model, removing access to the standard Flash and Pro models. The $4.99/month AI Plus subscription will be required for the standard Flash model, but it will no longer include Gemini Pro, which will be reserved for higher-tier AI Pro or Ultra subscribers costing $19.99 and $99.99 per month, respectively. Google says AI Plus subscribers will be notified by email about the loss of Gemini Pro access. Users can still select low, medium, and high effort levels for each model, though higher effort levels may consume usage limits faster. These changes reflect Google's restructuring of Gemini access tiers and subscription plans.

item.title: Mistral launches Le Chonk, a 1 trillion-parameter open-weight AI model optimized for coding and cyberdefense, claiming it is the most capable outside China [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: French AI company Mistral has released a preview of Le Chonk, a 1 trillion-parameter open-weight model designed for coding, cyberdefense, and specialized industry tasks. Mistral claims Le Chonk is the most capable open-weight model developed outside China and is competitive with proprietary models from the US and China. The final version is expected by the end of the month. Mistral emphasizes that Le Chonk was trained from scratch rather than using distillation techniques common in Chinese labs. The company aims to provide a cost-effective alternative to proprietary models, especially amid growing geopolitical tensions and restrictions on access to frontier AI models from US labs. Mistral's approach allows businesses to maintain control over their AI defenses without relying on closed models that may become unavailable.

item.title: Why OpenAI's Regulatory Nightmare Is Only Getting Started [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Imagine working in the OpenAI department responsible for dealing with politicians and regulators right now-things must be so intense you could almost be working for Elon Musk. Every politician worth their salt, in countries around the world, is jumping into the AI safety fray. Case in point: On Monday, the New York City Council, that bastion of AI expertise, held a hearing to discuss the risks that AI poses to humanity. The council called whistleblowers like former OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon to testify, along with officials from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta Platforms (Musk's SpaceX didn't show, and you can't blame them). OpenAI is also facing a U.S. Senate investigation spearheaded by Sen. Josh Hawley, not to mention a Federal Trade Commission inquiry and another one by the Australian government. The state of Florida has gone to court to make life miserable for OpenAI. The Europeans, of course, have gotten into the act with their own inquiry. And these are just the regulators!

item.title: Quoting Felix Rieseberg [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The "old" version of Cowork runs model inference in the cloud, executing tool calls in an Anthropic-provided VM we shipped to your computer. We added the VM for capability, safety, and security reasons - mapping in just the data you explicitly added to your session. People loved what they were able to do with Claude but didn't love the disk, battery, and performance cost of running the VM locally. Also, people didn't love that closing your laptop means the work stops. The "new" version of Cowork runs model inference and the VM in the cloud. Each session gets its own sandbox, not sharing state with other sessions. When the VM needs something on the users' device (like a file), the desktop app is responsible for that file access tool call. [...] We think this solves a lot of problems we've heard about (like using Cowork from a phone, keeping work running, or getting all the same power without losing battery to the VM) - Felix Rieseberg, Anthropic, see also this help page Tags: claude-cowork, anthropic, claude, generative-ai, ai, general-agents, llms
